# synology_quickconnect (Resource)

QuickConnect enabled policy, identifier, relay policy and complete service permissions. Import is required before any mutation. Synology account enrollment and browser/real-name consent remain in DSM. A successful configuration read does not prove external connectivity. Automatic router port forwarding is owned separately by synology_quickconnect_upnp. Destroy leaves QuickConnect and its registration unchanged.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "synology_quickconnect" "nas" {
  enabled       = true
  identifier    = "example-nas"
  relay_enabled = true
  services = {
    dsm_portal   = true
    mobile_apps  = true
    file_sharing = false
  }
}
import {
  to = synology_quickconnect.nas
  id = "quickconnect"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable QuickConnect using the existing Synology account binding.
- `identifier` (String) Customized QuickConnect ID. Omission preserves it; changing it requires enabled QuickConnect and an existing account binding.
- `relay_enabled` (Boolean) Allow use of Synology relay servers.
- `services` (Map of Boolean) Complete permission map keyed by DSM service identifier. Include all currently returned services; missing or unknown service IDs are refused rather than silently dropped.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Singleton import identity: quickconnect.
- `reconciliation_required` (Boolean) An interrupted configuration write requires DSM inspection and explicit release/import before another write.
- `registered_account` (String, Sensitive) Observed Synology account binding. This is configuration metadata and enters state; no account password or session is retained.
